title: API Design
subtitle: An API is a contract, and its shape sets the cost of every screen
motto: Shape the API for the caller
keyInsight: An API shaped like the database makes every screen pay in round trips and wasted bytes; shaping it for the caller moves that cost to the server.

decisions.title: Use one concrete screen as the workload
decisions.description: A user, their posts and each post's comments is a screen every reader can picture, and it exposes both round trips and over-fetching.
decisions.alternatives: An abstract request count is simpler but hides why one API style suits one caller and another suits a different one.

decisions.title: Include gRPC as the trade-off, not the winner
decisions.description: gRPC is fastest in the sim, but the frame says it cannot be called from a browser, so learners weigh fit against speed.
decisions.alternatives: Ranking the styles by speed alone would suggest gRPC everywhere, which is wrong for public web APIs.
